content.title: About
content.content: Tuna salad with Italian dressing is a ready‑to‑eat dish featuring cooked or canned tuna combined with vegetables, herbs, and a dressing made from olive oil, vinegar, and classic Italian seasonings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna is one of the richest sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart and brain health.
Italian dressing often includes oregano, basil, and garlic, giving the salad a Mediterranean aroma.
The salad is convenient for on‑the‑go meals: it requires no heating and stays tasty for several hours when refrigerated.
Canned tuna is usually packed in its own juice or oil, which influences the final calorie count of the salad.
In many countries, tuna salads are a traditional dish for summer picnics.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids help lower triglyceride levels and support vascular health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Tuna provides all essential amino acids, supporting muscle maintenance and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: The salad fits well into low‑carbohydrate diets and helps regulate blood sugar.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from veggies
items.content: Tomatoes, cucumbers, and greens add vitamin C and lycopene, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood may experience reactions to tuna.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned tuna often contains added salt; choose low‑sodium versions if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Mercury exposure
items.content: Tuna can contain trace amounts of mercury; moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Acidic dressing
items.content: The vinegar‑based dressing may irritate sensitive stomachs; reduce vinegar if needed.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a main dish or alongside bread, wraps, or rice. It stores well in an airtight container for lunch or picnics.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad refrigerated at 0–4 °C in a sealed container for up to 3 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
